userdoc.notice: Safe module that lets an agent key (never an owner) act for a Safe, only through Fengce. A refused call does not revert: it emits `Denied` and executes nothing, so blocked attempts are visible. Every agent call goes through `execTransactionFromModule`, where the Safe's module guard (the FengceGuard this executor is bound to) runs the circuit. The executor refuses to act if that guard is not the Safe's module guard. Agents can only make plain calls (no delegatecall). Adding an agent is a Safe transaction to this contract, so with FengceGuard installed it must be allowlisted (and after the first configuration, allowlist changes are timelocked). Revoking is immediate and can be done by the Safe or by any single owner.

userdoc.notice: Policy floors: a minimum rule (for example set by an organisation) that an account's own policy cannot go below. A floor is a pinned circuit with its own schema and bindings over the same policy context. For every evaluation the adapter (FengceGuard) calls `check`: the floor must be part of the account's policy (its circuit is in the policy's REF closure, verified once per policy with `verifyPolicy`), and the floor circuit must allow too. The decision is floor AND policy. Ownership: the account sets its floor once, naming the floor owner and a change delay (at least MIN_DELAY). From then on only the floor owner can change or remove the floor, and only after that delay. The account cannot detach this contract from its guard while a floor is set (FengceGuard asks `hasFloor`). Owners holding every signature can still remove the guard itself through recovery.

userdoc.notice: Safe v1.5.0 transaction guard and module guard that run every outgoing call through a pinned TapeOut circuit. One policy path serves both guards. A call is allowed only if the circuit's output bit 0 is 1; every error denies. Order of checks for a Safe transaction: 1. Delegatecall: only to MultiSendCallOnly 1.5.0; every inner call is checked as in step 4. 2. Call to this guard: recovery (all owners), timelock scheduling, configuration and allowlist    (free until the Safe is first configured, then timelocked). 3. Call to the Safe itself: installing this guard passes; any other guard or module guard needs    recovery; the other admin calls need the timelock; anything else is denied. 4. Anything else: decode facts (TxFacts), encode them with the Safe's schema, evaluate. Steps 2 and 3 make no call to the circuit, its processors or the pin registry.

userdoc.notice: Outcome checks: what a transaction actually did, not only what it said it would do. Before execution an adapter (FengceGuard on the owner and module paths, FengceHook for ERC-7579) calls `snapshot(account)`; after execution it calls `verify(account, success, policy)`. The Inspector records, in transient storage: - the balances of the account's watched assets (address(0) = native currency); - the account's allowances on those assets to its listed spenders; - a fingerprint of the account's owners, threshold, modules (first page), guard, module guard and   fallback handler. After execution it recomputes them: - any change to the fingerprint is denied outright (such changes must go through the admin path,   where adapters take no snapshot); - the total decrease of watched balances (`outflow`) and total increase of listed allowances   (`allowanceIncrease`) are passed to the account's policy as outcome facts (context version 2) through   `IFengcePolicy.checkContext`, which reverts unless the same circuit allows them. In this check the   transaction fields of the context are zero; the pre-execution check had the outcome fields at zero,   and both must allow. Nested checks (a module transaction made during an owner transaction) are counted; only the outermost snapshot and verification compare state, so the outer baseline cannot be replaced. Only adapters registered at construction may snapshot or verify, so a contract called during the transaction cannot reset or clear the baseline.

Domain verifier for Safe's ExtensibleFallbackHandler (v1.5.0) and FengceStrictHandler. Registered by a Safe for the Permit2 domain and for EIP-2612 token domains, it turns an off-chain approval the owners signed into approval facts, runs them through the Safe's Fengce policy, and only then checks the owners' signatures. Anything it does not recognise is rejected. Signature format (built by the signer, passed to `isValidSignature` by the protocol):   0x5fd7e97d ++ abi.encode(domainSeparator, typeHash, encodeData, payload)   payload = abi.encode(bytes data, bytes ownerSignatures)   - Permit2 PermitSingle: data = abi.encode(PermitDetails)   - Permit2 PermitBatch:  data = abi.encode(PermitDetails[])   - EIP-2612 Permit:      data = abi.encode(address token) ownerSignatures are Safe signatures (threshold) over the Safe message hash of the EIP-712 hash, exactly as Safe's default isValidSignature expects them.

userdoc.notice: "Strict Signatures" fallback handler for Safe v1.5.0. It is Safe's ExtensibleFallbackHandler (same fallback methods, token callbacks, ERC-165 and domain verifier settings, built from the same Safe v1.5.0 components) with one difference: `isValidSignature` has **no default path**. A signature is valid only if it targets a domain for which the Safe registered a verifier and that verifier accepts it. Plain owner signatures and approved hashes are refused, so an off-chain signature cannot move assets around the Fengce policy. Trade-off: dApps that rely on plain off-chain Safe signatures (for example sign-in messages or off-chain orders) stop working for this Safe; use on-chain approvals instead. Install with Safe.setFallbackHandler; with FengceGuard installed, changing the fallback handler or a domain verifier goes through the admin timelock.

userdoc.notice: Shared registry of approved TapeOut circuits (and plain contracts). A circuit pin records, from live chain state at pin time: the netlist hash, the hash of the full REF dependency closure, every processor in that closure with its code hash, and the circuit implementation behind the processors' beacon. `isPinned` re-reads the live values and fails closed (returns false, never reverts) on any difference or error. Stored netlists have no setter (TAP-02 section 3), so the closure is hashed once; what can still change is processor code, the beacon implementation, or the factory deregistering a processor. Pinning is permissionless: a pin id commits to its content, so nobody can squat or alter one.

userdoc.notice: State host for stateful (LATCH) TapeOut policies, evaluated with `step()` (TAP-02 section 4). Wallet-agnostic: an account (or the guard acting for it) asks Tick to advance a policy group before acting, and acts only if Tick returns. Groups: state belongs to a policy group, not to one account, so several Safes or agents can share one budget. A group fixes the stateful circuit (pinId), the reset period, and the schema + bindings that turn transaction facts into the circuit's input. Its admin (the creator) adds and removes member accounts. Only members can advance, directly or through a relayer they authorised (for example their FengceGuard, or a Chainlink CRE workflow). How state is stored: Tick keeps the circuit's state vector itself, per group, packed as TAP-02 bytes (bit i = bit i%8 of byte i/8). The circuit never stores anything. How state is reset: the period index is floor(block.timestamp / period) (Unix-epoch aligned); the first advance in a new period starts from the all-zero state. How it advances: step(state, input) runs; only if output bit 0 is 1 (allow) the new state is stored and the nonce incremented. A deny reverts and changes nothing. `expectedNonce` gives compare-and-swap for relayed calls (type(uint64).max skips the check). Rollback: the first advance of a group in a transaction snapshots its previous state; the same caller can `rollback` in that transaction (FengceGuard does this when the Safe transaction fails).

Decoder for UniswapV2Router02-style routers: swapExactTokensForTokens, swapTokensForExactTokens, swapExactETHForTokens, swapExactTokensForETH. Swap facts with token = path[0], tokenOut = path[last], recipient = to, deadline. For ETH input, amount = value.

Decoder for Uniswap SwapRouter02 (IV3SwapRouter, no deadline in the call): exactInputSingle, exactInput, exactOutputSingle, exactOutput. Swap facts: token = tokenIn, amount = amountIn (exact input) or amountInMaximum (exact output), tokenOut, minAmountOut = amountOutMinimum or the exact amountOut, recipient. SwapRouter02's recipient shortcuts are resolved: address(1) = the caller (the account), address(2) = the router itself.
